goals.0: Greetings for the time of day: Guten Morgen, Guten Tag, Guten Abend
goals.1: Asking how someone is, for friends and for strangers: du and Sie
goals.2: Polite and informal ways to say goodbye
goals.3: Addressing people with Herr and Frau before their names
dialog.1.de.4.n: Wie geht es …? — literally: how is it going?
dialog.1.de.6.n: Ihnen = the Dativ form of Sie; polite
dialog.3.de.0.n: Es geht = it's going — not very good, not bad
dialog.6.de.2.n: Wie geht's? = Wie geht es dir? — among friends
dialog.7.de.3.n: dir = the Dativ of du; Und dir? = And you?
dialog.9.de.0.n: Said before going to sleep, not when you meet
grammar.0.title: Which greeting when
grammar.0.note: Depending on the region you will also hear: Moin (northern Germany, all day), Servus (southern Germany and Austria), Grüß Gott (Bavaria and Austria). Learn to recognise them; for you, Guten Tag works everywhere.
grammar.1.title: Friend (du) or polite (Sie)?
grammar.1.note: When in doubt, choose the polite form (Sie); being too polite is never wrong.
grammar.2.title: Herr and Frau
grammar.2.text: Put Herr (man) or Frau (woman) before the name and use the surname: Herr Schmidt, Frau Becker. “Fräulein” is no longer used; say Frau for unmarried women too. At a first meeting, a handshake with eye contact is the normal custom.
quiz.3.prompt: What do you say politely in the evening?
quiz.3.why: When you meet in the evening: Guten Abend!
quiz.4.prompt: What do you say before going to sleep?
quiz.4.why: Gute Nacht! — before going to sleep or when saying goodbye at night.
quiz.5.prompt: How do you politely ask Mr Schmidt at the office how he is?
quiz.5.why: For strangers or in polite situations: Wie geht es Ihnen?
quiz.6.prompt: Which goodbye is natural with a close friend?
quiz.6.why: To a friend: Tschüss! or Bis bald!
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order to make the question: “How are you?” (polite)
